newsitem.title: UK: Cadbury sweetens market by stressing value.
newsitem.headline: Cadbury sweetens market by stressing value.

text.p: Cadbury Schweppes Plc pleased investors with a new commitment to emphasise shareholder value plus a convincing picture of growth potential for its soft drinks and confectionery businesses, analysts said on Wednesday.

The company's move to change its long term incentive plan to align management's motivation more closely to shareholders' interests was taken very positively by the market, they said. Cadbury's shares raced ahead to stand 19 pence higher at 529 pence by 1510 GMT.
The group also succeeded in soothing fears about intense competition in the U.S. soft drinks market, where Cadbury is up against Coca Cola and Pepsi.
"They have acknowledged they are in the ring with a couple of fearsome opponents," said David Laing at Henderson Crosthwaite, but they are saying that they can deal with it, he said.

Cadbury also seemed to succeed in convincing investors that distribution and bottling of its beverages in the U.S.-- their so called route to market -- was secure, despite some of its minor brands being delisted last year by Coca Cola.

Chief executive John Sunderland told a news conference on the group's annual results that the group was convinced that for the medium to long term its Dr Pepper brand had a secure place in all its routes to market in the United States.
"The company has strongly come out to allay fears over the U.S. route to market," said Ian Kellett, food manufacturing analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
Kellet said Kleinwort had recommended the stock as a "buy" and based on a multiple of 14.6 times for 1997, the shares looked relatively cheap.
Lang said the could be more to go for on the shares if Cadbury continued to deliver satisfactory volume results from its North American beverage operations.
"If Cadbury holds its own against Coke and Pepsi there's more to go for," he said.
